findings.summary: The README's tolerance figures understate Post: about 1%, not 0.5%, of the magnitude sums at the benchmark's largest size, and the per-pair term depends on the inputs
findings.detail: README, Specification ('So the accumulated float32 value is within about 0.5% of sum|P*dO| ... at every covered size') and Narrowings ('the tolerance stays below 0.5%'). 0.43% is only the accumulation factor (1 + rhoA)^516 - 1. The per-pair term of p16Err and ds16Err, the exponent's error, is about ln2*rH*aQK relative, and on the benchmark's own inputs (HEAD_DIM 128, randn, sm_scale 1.3, aQK about 150 to 270) it adds about 0.3 to 0.5%: at N_CTX = 2^14, on rows with real attention, dVTol is 0.8 to 1.1% of sum|P*dO|, dKTol 0.7 to 1.1% of sm_scale*sum|dS*Q|, and dQTol up to 2.2% of LN2*sum|dS*K| (work/premises.out; on rows that get little attention the absolute floors, such as N_CTX*eta16 per unit of |dO|, dominate). The term grows with aQK, which HeadV.Ok bounds only through xE + eX <= 15, so no fixed percentage holds at every covered size for every covered input. The Lean is right and the tolerance is meaningful on the host's inputs; the write-up should give the figure as a function of aQK (or say it is for inputs like the host's) and quote about 1% for the benchmark's largest size.
findings.evidence: work/premises.py simulates one head of the test's and the benchmark's inputs (forward M, o, delta, arg_k as the host computes them) and evaluates Spec.lean's formulas; work/premises.out has the figures.

findings.summary: The README's layout narrowing misdescribes the host's checks: do.is_contiguous() and equal strides already fix the contiguous strides on every dimension of size > 1
findings.detail: README, Narrowings: 'the host asserts only that the strides are equal ... a non-contiguous q with equal strides is not covered'. The host also asserts do.is_contiguous() (line 585) and q.stride() == ... == do.stride() (line 586), so q, arg_k, v, o and do have the contiguous strides on every dimension of size > 1. What the claim leaves out is a tensor whose size-1 dimension (BATCH = 1 or N_HEAD = 1) has a stride other than the canonical one, which torch's is_contiguous ignores; there stride_z or stride_h is multiplied by 0 and the kernel computes the same values, but model passes the canonical strides, so such a launch is not an instance. Suggest stating the narrowing that way.
findings.evidence: Source lines 585-586, 608-621; Model.lean model (strides H*N_CTX*HEAD_DIM, N_CTX*HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM, 1).

notes: No blocking finding. Model: every line of the three functions checked against SEMANTICS.md; work/names.out and names2.out print the model with full names (every operation TVA.*, the kernel's own helpers attn_bwd_dkdv and attn_bwd_dq; main's axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Value premises (HeadV.Ok) on the host's data (work/premises.out): benchmark at N_CTX = 2^14, HEAD_DIM 128, max (xE + eX) = 0.026 (causal 0.022) against 15, max pBr*yB = 14.8 against 2^15; test at N_CTX = 4096, max (xE + eX) = 0.0008 and max pBr*yB = 3.4; a HEAD_DIM 256 benchmark-style head 0.044 and 16.2. So the forward's M, the preprocess's delta and arg_k as the host makes them are covered with wide room. Optional: the proof's constants (pow_rhoA_le for T <= 1024, the 2^47 sums of sum_bd_le against the 2^50 cap of accI_dotAdd) appear to leave room for N_CTX <= 2^15, should a later round want to cover longer sequences than the benchmark's; not needed for the host's use.
